mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) contraction signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST < previous 3-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 YoY < -2% and HOUST falls below its 3-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when UNRATE exceeds 6.5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals a broad-based contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO declines by more than 0.5% for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp reduction in the federal funds rate below 2% during a recession signals an aggressive easing cycle, which lowers risk-free rates and boosts equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS falls below 2% and UNRATE exceeds 7%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (proxied by RSAFS growth > 1% for three consecutive months) combined with a flat or declining GDP (GDPC1 flat or falling for two consecutive quarters) signals a buildup of precautionary savings and weak demand, which depresses consumption and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth > 1% for three consecutive months AND GDPC1 flat or falling for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS grows >1% for three months and GDPC1 is flat or falling for two quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in payroll employment growth above 0.5% month-over-month for three consecutive months signals a robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS grows above 0.5% month-over-month for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 900K units for four consecutive months, coupled with a rising CPI (CPIAUCSL > previous 6-month average for three consecutive months), signals both weak housing demand and rising input costs, which compresses profit margins and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < 900K for four consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL > previous 6-month average for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when HOUST is below 900K for four months and CPIAUCSL exceeds its 6-month average for three consecutive months.
